findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities were removed and the label prior is equal-score, so no observed affinity outcome is available to either role.

The observed support is the learning window [0.0,0.5] with score nodes at 0.00-0.49 in 0.01 steps; the curve-support selection retained 24 features under a rule requiring absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05 and exclusion of a scale floor, with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE <= 0.35, zero strong sign-conflict nodes and quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1.

The information audit reports 14 independent batches and a compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS of about 0.081 A (CI95 ~0.070-0.092), with compressed-choice fixed RMS ~0.564 A and proper-rigid RMS ~0.529 A; the audit itself states these are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction, not a causal affinity effect.

Teacher-score correlations are weak and observational: compressed chosen-teacher score correlation ~0.102 (CI95 ~0.065-0.140) and full chosen-teacher score correlation ~0.064 (CI95 ~0.021-0.103), with top4 teacher overlap ~0.470; the audit explicitly flags these as not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.

Lineage support covers 14 complete-survival batches over 700 total batch nodes, but ancestral coverage is sparse: 349 nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch; terminal metadata show a single future-resampling node per batch at terminal score time 0.99 and state time 1.0, outside the observed window.

Continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear fits with extrapolation disallowed and polynomial fits not accepted; the inspected landmark features show multiple sign changes (4-10) and strong sign conflicts (1-9) with relative node RMSE from ~0.29 to ~0.78, so a constant rule is not supported and time-conditioned structure is not stably validated across the window.

hypotheses.falsifier: Contrast sign reverses or batch direction fraction falls below the selection threshold on held-out batches.
hypotheses.observable: signed coordinate contrast at observed selection nodes
hypotheses.statement: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts at observed selection nodes may carry directional information over the complete observed window, but the evidence supports only selection enrichment of a geometric descriptor, not an absolute geometric target or an affinity benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: Decoded terminal labels become available and show survival credit tracks final affinity.
hypotheses.observable: selection-node contrast versus descendant survival credit
hypotheses.statement: Immediate selection evidence and later survival/quality credit may disagree, and without decoded terminal labels last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the unavailable terminal-affinity comparison should be reported rather than substituted.

hypotheses.falsifier: A validated fit with accepted polynomial and low relative node RMSE and no strong sign conflicts.
hypotheses.observable: contrast value and local rate across observed nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule is not supported by the inspected continuous trends because fits are observed-node linear with extrapolation disallowed, polynomial fits rejected, and multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts present; a constant rule is likewise unsupported.

limitations: No current-study outcome data are supplied to the design roles; final predicted target affinity cannot be evaluated here.
Recorded affinities were removed and the label prior is equal-score, so no observed affinity label is available.

The information audit metrics are geometric nearest-teacher comparisons, not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect.
Teacher-score correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.
Terminal metadata lie outside the observed window (score time 0.99, state time 1.0), so last-record credit is not decoded terminal affinity benefit.
Ancestral coverage is sparse (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6), limiting lineage-based inference.
Continuous trends are observed-node linear with extrapolation disallowed and polynomial fits rejected; sign changes and strong sign conflicts prevent a stable constant or time-conditioned rule.
No joint covariance, intact-conformation or mode diagnostics were read, so coherent joint-pattern versus isolated-marginal comparison is not supported by the evidence read.
No population-contrast versus parent-child increment turnover comparison was read, so within-path change versus changing cohort composition is not resolved here.
